catalog_quote: [p.545] For the description of the Palaung word it is necessary to distinguish two types of syllable, which will be referred to as major and minor syllables. ... a major syllable is one which contains a vowel, a minor syllable containing no vowel other than an anaptyctic one, represented in the transcription by ə. With the exception of a small number of loanwords, and of the proolitic particles mentioned in the next paragraph, all Palaung words consist of a major syllable which may be preceded by one or two minor syllables. Symbolizing major syllables by (Ma) and minor ones by (Mi), the possible structures are thus : Monosyllable (Ma) e.g. ta? ' to weave ' Disyllable (MiMa) e.g. korta? sweep_summary: Shwe Palaung (shwe1236) is in the catalog as fixed-unreviewed (final/major-syllable prominence, Shorto 1960). this search of works with stress in the title's two Glottolog title-hits — Butt, Bögel & Jabeen 2017 (LFG'17, open PDF downloaded and read: Urdu/Hindi polar kya, 0 mentions of Palaung) and Butt, Jabeen & Bögel 2020 (De Gruyter, DOI 10.1515/9783110650532-004, paywalled; title names Urdu/Hindi) — are both mis-linked to shwe1236: Glottolog's records state the language link is a 'computerized assignment from "kya"'. Both are other-language items, silent on the catalog, priority none. Semantic Scholar API could not be reached by automated download; a Crossref title query for 'Palaung stress' surfaced no new stress source beyond Shorto 1960 (the catalog's own deciding source) plus non-stress Palaung items (Ostapirat-era 'Dara'ang Palaung' handbook chapter DOI 10.1163/9789004283572_024 is a different variety and not a stress title). sources.citation: Milne, Leslie (1921). An Elementary Palaung Grammar. Oxford: Clarendon Press. 198 pp.
sources.note: Milne 1921 makes no statement about word stress, so it neither supports nor contradicts the catalog's final/major-syllable prominence (Shorto 1960). Shorto 1960 p.544 says so explicitly: 'Mrs. Milne gave no account of the phonology of Palaung, and of the phonetics only some summary remarks explaining the symbols of her transcription' (copy consulted). An earlier screen had read the p.12 sentence 'each syllable stands alone, clear and distinct' as 'no word stress'; read in context (it closes the list of letter pronunciations and vowel-length diacritics) it is about syllable articulation and do…
